title: Government Schemes and Current Affairs of Assam

blocks.content: Government Schemes and Current Affairs of Assam

Covers major state government welfare schemes — a fast-changing area given periodic scheme launches/upgrades, so this chapter emphasizes the framework and most current verified details as of writing; always cross-check exact figures against the latest official announcement before an exam.

items: Orunodoi (also spelt Arunodoi) is Assam's flagship direct cash-transfer welfare scheme, launched on 2nd October 2020, providing monthly financial assistance to economically weaker households via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), with women as the primary beneficiaries/account holders.
The scheme began with a monthly benefit of ₹830, subsequently increased to ₹1,250 per month under later phases.

Orunodoi 3.0, launched in 2025, expanded coverage to approximately 38–40 lakh households and added an additional LPG subsidy component (₹250/month from January 2026 under the Mukhyamantri Sulabh Indhan Asoni, bringing the total combined monthly benefit to ₹1,500) alongside the base ₹1,250 monthly transfer.

Eligible beneficiary categories under Orunodoi include women heads of economically weaker households, widows, divorced/separated women, and women with certain critical illnesses, among other specified criteria — exact eligibility criteria should be verified from the current official scheme guidelines.

Mukhya Mantrir Nijut Moina Scheme — a flagship scheme providing monthly financial assistance to girl students to boost enrolment and retention in higher education and reduce school dropout rates; Nijut Moina 2.0, launched in 2025, expanded the scheme's scope and beneficiary coverage across several hundred colleges statewide.

Arundhati Gold Yojana — provides financial assistance (in the form of gold/its monetary equivalent) to support marriage expenses for eligible brides, a scheme aimed at reducing the financial burden of marriage-related expenses on families.
Mukhyamantri Mahila Udyamita Abhiyaan (MMUA) — aimed at promoting women's entrepreneurship through financial and other support mechanisms.

Multiple schemes specifically target tea garden worker welfare, including wage compensation for pregnant workers and dedicated health insurance coverage, reflecting the tea industry's continued social and economic significance in the state.
Atmanirbhar Asom Abhijan — a broader self-reliance mission encompassing skill development, rural infrastructure, and self-employment initiatives.
Apun Ghar / Aponar Apon Ghar schemes — provide home loan subsidies/support, targeting both state government employees and the general population respectively, to promote affordable housing access.
Jibon Prerana — a scheme aimed at supporting young graduates, reflecting the state's focus on youth employment and entrepreneurship.

Given the pace at which welfare schemes are launched, renamed, or upgraded (e.g., Orunodoi's progression through multiple version numbers), candidates should treat this chapter as a framework for understanding scheme categories, and always verify exact current figures, eligibility, and scheme names against recent official Assam government notifications before an exam.

cells:
Exam Tip

• Orunodoi is the single most heavily tested current-affairs scheme in Assam GS papers given its scale and political prominence — know its launch date, current monthly benefit amount, and most recent version/expansion details precisely.

• Scheme-to-target-group matching (Nijut Moina → girl students, Arundhati Gold Yojana → marriage support, MMUA → women entrepreneurs) is a common question format.

• Given schemes are frequently updated, treat any specific rupee figures or dates in this chapter as a snapshot — always verify against the latest official source close to your actual exam date.
